title: The Workspaces feature captures the opened tabs but the contents like tabs in browsers and path in command prompts are missing when it is launched
summary: Workspaces restores browser and command-prompt windows but not their private in-app tab contents or prior working paths; a maintainer explains this is an intentional privacy boundary and suggests CLI arguments.

judgment.rationale: The issue asks Workspaces to capture browser tab contents and command-prompt state. The maintainer explains that extracting arbitrary running-app content could let third-party apps read other apps' state and gives a per-workspace CLI-argument workaround. The report supplies no regression in supported snapshot behavior or safe app-specific restore contract.
evidence: The report uses Chrome tabs and command prompts launched from a specific path; after capture, content/history and paths are not restored.
A maintainer explains Workspaces cannot obtain arbitrary application contents for privacy/security reasons and suggests setting CLI args in the workspace editor.
Timeline cross-references #35448 and #36005, both closed; neither proves a fix for arbitrary application session restoration.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep the documented CLI-argument workaround; reconsider only with a safe supported app-specific interface.

fix_assessment.rationale: The requested generic capture crosses an explicit product privacy boundary; no safe supported app-specific contract or regression is supplied, so a generic fix does not apply.
